# CANDIDATE: RIBBON_SQUEEZE_BREAKOUT

**Filed:** 2026-07-09  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

When the EMA ribbon contracts tightly (ribbon width < 0.5×ATR(14) for three consecutive 5‑min bars) and price breaks out on expanding volume (close > EMA20 with volume >1.3× the average 5‑min volume of the prior 20 bars), the ensuing move tends to persist. This edge exists because volatility contraction often precedes expansion, and a breakout with volume confirmation indicates institutional participation.

## Mechanism

- Compute ribbon width = |EMA9 − EMA50| on 5‑min bars.
- If ribbon width < 0.5×ATR(14) for three consecutive bars, and the next bar closes > EMA20 with volume >1.3× the average 5‑min volume of the prior 20 bars, enter long at the bar's close (short symmetric with opposite conditions: ribbon width < 0.5×ATR(14) for three consecutive bars, next bar closes < EMA20 with volume >1.3× average volume, enter short).
- Exit: Chart-stop at the opposite side of the ribbon (for long, below EMA50; for short, above EMA9). TP1 at 2R (twice the risk from entry to stop). Runner: trail 10% off the high-water mark (for long) or low-water mark (for short) after TP1 is hit.
